title: legal-redlines-scratchpad-emma-rodriguez
content:
Legal redline notes — scratchpad
Owner: Emma Rodriguez (legal)
Status: working notes / negotiation talking points
Last updated: 2026-03-02

Notes to self / context:
- This is my running scratchpad for customer contract redlines where inference/model usage/data processing are involved. Keep things concise for AE/AM to use in negotiations.
- Focus areas: data use (training), IP/outputs, indemnity/liability, SLA/credits/termination, security & audit scope, export controls, model-specific carve-outs.
- Typical customer types: SaaS product teams, regulated enterprise (healthcare/finance/government).

High-level negotiating posture (Redwood):
- We need to avoid any language that gives customers rights over model weights, training pipelines, underlying model IP. Customer gets broad rights to use outputs for their business but not to claim ownership of the model.
- Try to keep indemnity narrow: Redwood accepts IP indemnity for service-delivered infringement (software service), but not for customer data-derived claims or third-party model providers. Consider mutuality where feasible for enterprise deals.
- Liability cap = standard (fees paid in prior 12 months) with carveouts for gross negligence, willful misconduct, and IP indemnity. Consider higher cap for strategic enterprise deals.
- No right for the vendor to train models on customer confidential data without explicit opt-in (customer consent + DPA).

Clause-by-clause notes / redline suggestions:
1) Definitions: "Customer Data", "Service Data", "Model Outputs"
- Define explicitly: Customer Data = data provided/ingested by customer (prompts, files). Service Data = logs, telemetry, aggregated usage (non-identifiable). Model Outputs = text generated by the service in response to customer input.
- Suggest add: "Model Outputs shall be considered Customer Data for the purposes of data return/deletion obligations." (Risk: customers may try to assert IP over model internals if outputs used to fine-tune models — see training below.)

2) Data processing / Training on customer data
- Redline: "Vendor shall not use Customer Data, including Model Outputs, to train or improve models or for model development unless Customer provides prior written consent and a separate addendum (Training Addendum)."
- Negotiation fallback: allow anonymized, aggregated telemetry for product improvement, but explicitly exclude prompts and model outputs containing PII.
- Risk: enterprise customers often require strict no-training/no-derivative clauses — use DPA to address retention, deletion, and purpose limitation.

3) IP ownership and license grants
- Customer owns Customer Data.
- Grant back: Customer grants Redwood a limited, revocable license to process Customer Data to provide the service, to improve service per opt-in, and to store/retain logs as described.
- Outputs: propose language "Customer shall own and have exclusive rights to Model Outputs generated solely from Customer Data and the Service; Redwood retains the model and all underlying technology and weights."
- Watch for customer ask: claim ownership of model outputs + right to compel training — push back, allow outputs ownership but restrict training without consent.

4) Confidentiality
- Standard: 3–5 years for most confidential info; perpetual for trade secrets.
- For AI-specific: flag prompts that may contain customer secrets — treat prompts and outputs as confidential if labeled so by customer; otherwise treat as Customer Data.

5) Indemnity
- Redwood to indemnify for claims that the Service (excluding Customer Data or Customer-provided content) infringes third-party IP.
- Exclude: claims arising from Customer Data, combination of Service with third-party tech, open-source components used as permitted, or modifications by customer.
- Customer indemnity: customer indemnifies for claims arising from Customer Data, customer content, or customer misuse (including violation of use restrictions).
- Ask for mutual limitation: Redwood's indemnity should be commercial-in-confidence and capped (linked to liability cap) where possible.

6) Limitation of Liability
- Typical: exclude consequential, special, punitive damages. Cap direct damages at the greater of $1M or fees paid in prior 12 months (or 12 months' fees) — for enterprise deals we can negotiate higher caps.
- Carveouts: IP indemnity, breaches of confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct.

7) SLA, uptime and credits
- Define clear SLO and remedy: service credits only, no termination right for single incident unless repeated underperformance.
- If customer pushes for termination rights or higher penalties, require objective metrics and minimum cure periods.
- Add guardrail: cumulative credits capped (e.g., 50% of monthly fees) and credits as sole remedy.

8) Termination & Survival
- Termination for convenience: Redwood prefers 30 days notice for customers; customers often request 90 days. Be flexible for larger contracts.
- Termination for cause: immediate for material breach after short cure period (e.g., 30 days).
- Survival: IP ownership, confidentiality, indemnities, liability cap survive as usual.

9) Audit rights / SOC2 / security certifications
- Customers request broad audit rights; push back: provide SOC2 Type II report, summary security posture, and limited audit rights (on-site only for high-risk customers with NDA and expense sharing).
- Security obligations: maintain SOC2, implement encryption at rest/in transit, key management options (customer-managed KMS for Private deployments).
- Incident response: notify within 72 hours of a confirmed incident; provide remediation plan.

10) Data deletion and return
- On termination, return or delete Customer Data within X days (30–60). For hosted customers, provide retention schedule and deletion certificate on request.
- For Private deployments, clarify process and support for secure wipes.

11) Export control / sanctions / prohibited use
- Standard export control clause. Add callouts for sensitive verticals (healthcare PHI, government data) and require customer to confirm compliance.

12) Subcontracting and assignment
- Redwood wants freedom to subcontract (e.g., cloud infra, model providers). Add requirement: Redwood remains liable for subcontractors.
- Assignment: allow assignment to affiliates or in M&A; require notice to customer for assignment to unrelated third party.

13) Insurance
- Typical ask: maintain general liability, cyber/privacy insurance (e.g., $2M–5M). For enterprise customers, they may request higher limits — escalate to BizDev/AM.

14) Fees, payment terms, taxes
- Net30 standard. Add late fee interest (1.5%/month) and allow suspension for non-payment after notice.
- Taxes: customer pays VAT/GST unless vendor required to collect.

15) AI-specific safety / acceptable use
- Include usage restrictions (illegal activities, PII scraping, targeted disinformation). Right to suspend accounts for misuse.
- Consider adding review & escalation path for safety incidents.

Negotiation playbook / talking points (short):
- If customer pushes to train on their data: ask for separate paid "Private Training" addendum, strict DPA, and opt-in key-management controls.
- If they demand ownership of outputs + training rights: accept ownership of outputs but refuse training rights unless paid/contracted. Offer a revenue-share or pilot for training use.
- If customer wants low liability cap: push to link cap to fees paid in prior 12 months; for strategic deals, accept higher cap but with indemnity carveouts and insurance proof.
- For SLA termination demands: insist on objective metrics, cure periods, and cap credits.

Quick redline language snippets (to paste into contract):
- Data/training opt-out: "Vendor shall not use Customer Data or Model Outputs to train, tune, or otherwise improve Vendor models, unless Customer provides explicit prior written consent via a separate Training Addendum."
- Outputs ownership: "Customer shall own Model Outputs; Vendor retains ownership of models, weights, and underlying algorithms. Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Model Outputs for its business purposes."
- Liability cap: "Except for liability arising from (i) Vendor's breach of confidentiality obligations, (ii) Vendor's gross negligence or willful misconduct, or (iii) Vendor's indemnification obligations with respect to third-party intellectual property, Vendor's total aggregate liability to Customer shall not exceed the greater of (A) the fees paid by Customer to Vendor under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, or (B) $1,000,000."

Open items / TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm standard liability cap for enterprise deals with finance (is $1M floor acceptable?). See ticket: JIRA-LEGAL-1021.
- [ ] Update DPA template with explicit no-training clause and KMS opt-in options.
- [ ] Create short AM cheat-sheet (1 pager) with 3–4 negotiation bullets for customers wanting training or ownership.
- [ ] Sync with product on telemetry retention defaults (30/90/365 days) and options for customers to shorten.

Recent examples / reference points:
- Customer A (healthcare): insisted on no training + 3-year data deletion certificate + SOC2 + on-site audit rights. Resolved by providing SOC2 + limited audit + explicit DPA no-training clause.
- Customer B (large fintech): asked for unlimited liability for data breach — unacceptable. Escalated to legal + finance; offered increased insurance requirement + higher liability cap limited to actual damages.

Handy links: Confluence contract templates (see linked artifacts).

Notes on tone: keep public-facing contract language as concise and principle-based as possible; detailed technical controls can live in DPA/Exhibit. For driven negotiations, emphasize risk allocation and operational mitigations (KMS, private deployment, SOC2).

End of scratchpad.

-- Emma
